items.prompt:
Climate is
A) the usual weather of a place over many years
B) the weather on one day
C) a type of rock
D) a kind of animal
items.answer: A) the usual weather of a place over many years

steps: Climate is the long-term typical weather.

items.prompt:
Do different regions have different climates?
A) Yes
B) No
C) Only in summer
D) Only deserts

steps: Climates vary from region to region.

items.prompt:
Near the equator, the climate is usually
A) cold and snowy
B) hot all year
C) very dry only
D) windy only

steps: Equator regions are usually hot all year.

items.prompt:
A desert's climate is
A) warm and very rainy
B) very dry with little rain
C) cold and snowy all year
D) always windy
items.answer: B) very dry with little rain

items.prompt:
Why combine information from several sources about climate?
A) To get a fuller, more complete description
B) To hide facts
C) To change the climate
D) There is no reason
items.answer: A) To get a fuller, more complete description

steps: Combining sources gives a more complete picture.

items.prompt:
Weather and climate are
A) the same thing
B) different, because weather is day to day and climate is long-term
C) both only about rain
D) both one day long
items.answer: B) different, because weather is day to day and climate is long-term

steps: Weather is short-term; climate is the long-term pattern.

items.prompt:
A rainforest and a desert have very different climates because
A) they look the same
B) the rainforest is warm and very rainy while the desert is very dry
C) both are cold
D) both get no rain
items.answer: B) the rainforest is warm and very rainy while the desert is very dry

steps: Their long-term rainfall and warmth differ greatly.

items.prompt:
A temperature chart and a rainfall map together can describe a climate because they show
A) only the date
B) how warm and how wet a region usually is
C) the price of land
D) the names of animals
items.answer: B) how warm and how wet a region usually is

steps: Temperature plus rainfall describes the climate.
